Your result
Your list is the problem
You already have a way to send. What you don't have is a reason to believe the people receiving it care this week. That's the part we built: intent signals first, messages second.
An autonomous agent fits you
With nobody writing outbound today, a full agent like 11x or Agent Frank buys you the most time. Come to us instead if you'd rather fix who gets contacted before you automate the contacting.
Buy sending, not an agent
Deliverability and cost are your constraints, so Instantly or Smartlead will serve you better than any AI SDR. Come to us instead when the sending works and the replies still don't.
Table of contents
Four picks before the long list, by where outbound hurts.
Gojiberry
Best when the problem is who you contact, not how fast. Flat rate per account.
Apollo.io
Best when you want a database and sequencing on one bill, with a rep driving.
Instantly
Best when the job is email volume at the lowest monthly cost.
Reply.io
Best when email, calls and social share one cadence, with a human approving.

Five reasons come up, price being the loudest. The quieter one is data: median job tenure in the US runs 3.9 years, with 22% of workers in post under a year, so a chunk of any list you inherited already points at people who've moved on.
Our guide to B2B sales automation covers where each layer sits in the stack.

These twelve don't do the same job. Three are agents running outbound end to end, seven are platforms where a rep drives, one is a set of parts you wire together. The first starts earlier, by deciding who's worth a message. The order runs from closest swaps to cheapest pieces.

How we built this list. Every price was read off the vendor's own pricing page in September 2026. We ignored the figures circulating in comparison posts, several of which describe a model that doesn't exist any more, and where a vendor gates its numbers we say so.

What you won't find is a scorecard of reply rates. We haven't run one campaign on one list through all twelve, and a made-up percentage would be worth less than this sentence admitting it. We pay for every plan ourselves, no vendor read this first, and Gojiberry is our product, which is why it's first and why we say where it loses.

Gojiberry watches for the moment a company starts looking, then reaches the people inside it. It tracks 30+ buying-intent signals across socials and the web, scores them against your ICP, and runs the outreach. You're buying the list; sending is what happens next.
Pro is $99 a month for the account, not per seat, with two agents and up to 1,800 prospects contacted. There's a free start.
We won't pretend to be the hands-off agent AiSDR sells. We make sure the 400 people you contact are worth contacting: GTE Localize booked 100+ meetings that way, and you can read how.
11x runs Alice, an agent that researches accounts, writes the touches, sends them, and handles what comes back. Outbound happens without anyone opening a sequence builder.
Growth starts at $3,750 a month on annual billing. Pro and Enterprise aren't published, they're quoted.
It removes more manual work than anything here, and it's a first-year commitment costing what a junior rep does.
Artisan bundles a 300M+ database with Ava, an agent that builds sequences and runs them. Autopilot sends alone, copilot waits for approval.
The Employee package lists around $600 a month billed annually, and you won't see volume pricing without a call.
One vendor instead of three. Then you notice the annual term, and that what's published is a floor.
Agent Frank pulls prospects from a 500M+ index, writes in your tone, sends and follows up. It works in 20+ languages, which counts once your market stops being English-only.
Frank starts at $599 a month billed quarterly for 1,000 active contacts, and you'll get two months free annually.
No buying signals sit underneath, so Frank writes beautifully to whoever you've pointed him at. Plenty of teams take that trade.
Reply.io has run sequences since 2014, with Jason AI added on top. Email, calls, SMS and social share one cadence, and a rep signs off.
Email Volume opens at $49 per user a month, Multichannel at $89, plus channel add-ons. Jason AI's separate, from $500.
Human oversight is where it wins. Per-seat arithmetic is where it loses.
Regie.ai stacks AI agents on a 220M+ database, with sequencing, intent prioritization and a dialer. It's aimed at sales floors rather than founders.
AI SEP lists at $180 per user a month with a ten-seat minimum, so the real floor's $1,800 a month.
The seat minimum decides this one. Below ten reps with nobody owning ops, the contract costs more than the pipeline it'd find you.
Amplemarket puts contact data, buying signals and sequencing behind one login, with an AI copilot reviewing campaigns. Teams that move here retire three or four subscriptions.
Startup is $600 a month for two seats, annual billing only. Growth and Elite aren't published at all.
Nothing here folds more tools into one contract, and nothing here asks a two-person team for a bigger bet before they've tested it.
Apollo is the first subscription many small teams buy: database, sequences, dialer and CRM sync in one workspace. A rep drives all of it.
Basic runs $49 per seat on annual billing, Professional $79, Organization $119 with three seats minimum. Pay monthly and you'll add 20%.
It's the cheapest route to data and sending on one subscription, if somebody has the hours to work it.
Instantly exists to get cold email delivered at volume. Unlimited sending accounts and warmup come with every plan, so the bill tracks sends rather than headcount.
Growth is $47 a month for 5,000 sends, Hypergrowth $97, Light Speed $358. The lead database isn't bundled, it's billed apart.
Nothing here moves more email for less money. Then you add credits and the CRM module, and $47 lands nearer $125.
Clay is a table where each column calls a data provider or an AI agent. 150+ sources sit behind it, and nothing sends until you attach a sender.
Launch is $185 a month with 2,500 data credits and Growth is $495. New customers can't buy the old tiers.
Ceiling is the highest here. Floor is a person who wants to build.
Smartlead sells deliverability: unlimited mailboxes, warmup, inbox rotation and a master inbox, pointed at agencies and high-volume senders.
Base is $39 a month for 2,000 leads and 6,000 sends, Pro $94, Unlimited Smart $174, Prime $379. You aren't charged per inbox.
Nothing here protects a sending reputation better, and nothing here cares less whether the list deserved the send.
Snov.io folds an email finder, verifier, drip campaigns and a light CRM into one cheap subscription. Seats are unlimited on every paid plan.
Starter is $39 a month for 1,000 credits and Pro starts at $99 for 5,000. Social automation isn't included, at $69 per slot.
Price is the whole argument. A three-person team gets a full outbound loop for less than one Apollo seat, and depth is what they pay for it.
Monthly starting prices, taken from each vendor directly in September 2026. Seat minimums and annual-only terms are flagged where they move the floor.

For warm, high-intent leads, it's us. Claiming otherwise would be odd, since finding them is why Gojiberry exists. Wispra now sources 60% of its weekly demos from intent signals, which you can see broken down here.

For a fully autonomous rep, 11x if the budget and security review are there, Artisan if you'd rather one vendor carried the data. On budget, Instantly wins on the sticker and Snov.io once you count seats. For all-in-one prospecting, Apollo, whose free plan lets you find out before committing.
For multichannel with oversight, Reply.io. For personalization, Clay, if somebody enjoys building. For deliverability at volume, Smartlead. For a bigger SDR floor, Regie.ai past ten seats.
Want better leads before you start sending?
Gojiberry surfaces prospects who are in-market this week and enriches them before they reach your sequences.
Four questions settle most of it, and the last decides less than people expect.

Your stack, ICP and volume matter more than any feature table. Volume without targeting is also the shortest path to Google's 0.3% spam complaint threshold, which bulk senders have had to stay under since February 2024. Our walkthrough on automating sales prospecting orders those decisions.

Smartlead's Base plan and Snov.io's Starter both open at $39 a month, and Instantly's Growth at $47. None of the three includes an agent. Gojiberry's Pro plan is $99 for the whole account, with nothing charged per seat.

A team of two to ten wants flat pricing and no seat minimums, which points at Gojiberry, Instantly, Smartlead and Snov.io. Regie.ai's ten-seat minimum and Amplemarket's annual-only contract rule both out at that size.
Not the whole job. Agents handle research, first touches and follow-ups well, and they're weak on objections. Teams that get value from them move reps toward closing rather than cutting heads.

Instantly or Smartlead, and it's close. Smartlead's rotation and master inbox are more mature, Instantly is cheaper at entry. Both make you bring a list, and B2B contact data decays around 2.1% a month.

Reply.io if you want a rep approving each step, Gojiberry if you'd rather the agent coordinate email and social itself. Reply's add-ons push the real per-seat cost near $187, so run that against your headcount.

Apollo, Clay and Snov.io all run free tiers, and each one's a demo rather than a working plan. Gojiberry starts free without a card, AiSDR has no trial at all. Our roundup of email outreach automation tools covers each tier.

If you want a lighter commitment, better data control, or an intent-first approach, there are strong alternatives. Below are 12 options, from AI-powered prospecting to data giants and outreach engines, with an honest breakdown of each.
Artisan or Gojiberry?
3 quick questions to see which tool actually fits your real outbound needs.

Gojiberry is an AI-powered, multi-channel prospecting platform. It tracks 30+ buying-intent signals across socials and the web, surfaces leads who are in-market right now, and triggers personalized outreach across channels. Its core strength is turning a dynamic market into a predictable pipeline: it monitors real-time buying signals and filters them through your ICP, so the leads you get are pre-qualified opportunities, not just a list of contacts.

For sales teams, that means sequences populated with prospects who just started a new role, engaged a competitor post, or work at a company that just raised funding · timing that lifts reply rates. For founders, it identifies early adopters and decision-makers in your niche without hiring a full-time SDR.
Best for
Founders and B2B sales teams who want warm, in-market leads without building an autonomous stack.
Free starter for your first warm leads; Pro at $99/mo per account; Elite and Custom for larger teams.
Flagship autonomous AI SDR.

For enterprise teams betting on full autonomy, it is a direct, same-weight-class alternative to Artisan · with the usual autonomous trade-offs around personalization depth.
Enterprise orgs committed to fully autonomous outbound.
Enterprise, quote-based.
Gojiberry finds prospects the moment they show buying intent, filters them through your ICP, and delivers them warm · so outreach lands at the right time.
All-in-one data plus outreach.
Apollo bundles a 275M+ contact database with native sequences and a dialer, so you consolidate data, enrichment and engagement affordably.
Build a precise list in minutes, reveal verified emails and dials, then enroll contacts into sequences without leaving the platform. A generous free tier helps you test first.

Pairing its data with a sequencer like Outreach or Salesloft is a classic high-performance stack, though it is a significant investment.
Established teams needing an enterprise data partner.
Quote-based, annual.
AI power inside a familiar engine.

Reply.io injects AI into a robust sales-engagement platform. Its Jason AI feature acts like an AI SDR with autopilot and copilot modes, so it feels like an upgrade to your current engine rather than a whole new one.
Transparent pricing and unlimited users on AI SDR plans lower per-seat cost, with smooth onboarding and deliverability and warmup tools out of the box.
Teams wanting AI prospecting inside a familiar SEP.
Volume/active-contacts; AI SDR plans available.
Deliverability and creative personalization.
lemlist delivers emails to the primary inbox and is famous for lemwarm, its built-in warmup, plus creative personalization like dynamic images, videos and landing pages.
A clean UI and an active community make it easy to launch fast. It needs more hands-on management than a fully autonomous AI SDR, but gives you full control over messaging.
Teams prioritizing reply rates and creative outreach.
From $59/mo; multichannel on higher tiers.
Composable enrichment and workflows.

Ops-heavy teams building a composable stack.
Credit-based.
CRM-native engagement.

Trigger sequences from CRM properties, website activity or forms to build contextual outreach, scaling from free tools to enterprise forecasting.
Teams on (or adopting) HubSpot CRM.
Freemium, then seat-based.
Enterprise execution command center.

Outreach is the heavyweight for established teams enforcing a consistent process across many reps: multi-channel sequences with triggers, the Kaia assistant for call coaching, and deal-health analytics.
It is an operating system for revenue teams · powerful, but a bigger lift and investment than a lightweight tool.
Large revenue orgs needing consistent process.
Quote-based, enterprise.
Engagement with coaching and governance.
Salesloft orchestrates cadences, a dialer, conversation intelligence and forecasting, so managers coach on real interactions, not just activity.
Role-based permissions and deep bi-directional CRM sync keep data integrity across the go-to-market motion.
Mid-market to enterprise focused on coaching.
Enterprise pricing.
High-volume cold email at scale.
Instantly is engineered for high-volume cold email, letting you connect and warm unlimited inboxes without paying per mailbox · a standout for agencies running big campaigns.
A workspace model with generous, add-on-expandable limits keeps pricing transparent and scalable.
Agencies and high-volume senders.
Growth/Hypergrowth tiers.
Budget-friendly all-in-one outreach.
Snov.io combines an email finder, verification, multichannel outreach and a light CRM at an accessible price · ideal for startups and SMBs.
A credit-based model, unlimited campaigns and built-in warmup help small teams scale outbound affordably.
Startups and SMBs on a budget.
Low-cost credit tiers.

The best fit depends on your real constraint: budget, data accuracy, deliverability control, or how much you want automated end to end. A bundled AI BDR is convenient but locks your data and sending into one vendor; a modular or intent-first approach trades some convenience for control and timing.
Is your problem data or copy?
If campaigns bounce or get no replies, it is almost always data. Fix that first · it is cheaper than any AI agent.
How hands-off do you want to be?
Want truly hands-off? Stay in the AI SDR camp. Want control and timing? Go intent-first or modular.
How important is avoiding lock-in?
If you want portable data and freedom to swap tools, a modular or intent-first stack wins over a bundled BDR.
What is your budget?
Under a few hundred a month rules out full-stack AI SDRs. Intent-first and data-plus-outreach tools fit smaller budgets.
Skip the bundled lock-in and get straight to warm, in-market prospects. Gojiberry finds the intent signals and delivers pre-qualified leads. Free trial, no credit card required.

Usually price, data control and lock-in. Artisan targets funded teams, and its bundled data and sending live inside one vendor · convenient until you find gaps in your niche or want to swap the data provider or own your deliverability. Fully automated copy can also drift generic at scale.

An autonomous AI SDR like Artisan or 11x runs outreach end to end with minimal input. An intent-first tool like Gojiberry focuses on who to contact and when · surfacing prospects the moment they show buying intent, then enriching them for your outreach. It depends on your constraint. A modular stack (a data or intent layer, an outreach tool, and your CRM) is often cheaper and more controllable than a bundled AI BDR, and avoids lock-in. If you genuinely want hands-off, a full-stack AI SDR may be worth the premium.

ZoomInfo publishes no prices at all, and every quote goes through a sales conversation before you see a number.
The median signed contract sits at $33,500 a year, based on more than 1,500 purchases aggregated by Vendr in 2026.
ZoomInfo never says how many seats a plan includes. It only says paid plans carry a seat minimum, and that's worth knowing before the call.

You can't find the price because ZoomInfo doesn't put one anywhere. The official pricing page is a contact form. Their own blog post on what the product costs runs about twenty minutes of reading and gives you no figure at the end of it.

So this page gathers what buyers report paying, what makes a quote climb once the call starts, and the team size at which that spend starts to pay for itself. Every number here is attributed in the sentence that carries it, because none of them come from ZoomInfo's own price list.
Gojiberry finds your prospects for you
ZoomInfo sells you access to a database. Gojiberry watches more than 30 buying signals and tells you which accounts are worth contacting right now, for 99 dollars a month.
Table of contents

Plan names tell you less than headcount does, because the platform fee is only the starting point and seats stack on top of it. Here's what teams report spending across a full year, seats and the usual extras included.
ZoomInfo bills annually. The invoice covers twelve months and it's paid upfront.
There is no monthly subscription, and no self-serve checkout that would let you start small and grow into it.
If you see a monthly figure quoted on another site, that's an annual price divided by twelve so it reads better in a budget. It isn't a way to pay.

Yes, and the free tier is real rather than a trial with a countdown on it. ZoomInfo rewrote its pricing content on 7 August 2026 to push exactly this message, so anyone landing on the site now meets a free-to-start offer before meeting a rep.
Here's what ZoomInfo Lite includes, according to ZoomInfo.

Put 10 credits back in perspective before you plan anything around them. Ten credits a month means ten contact records downloaded, which is a sample rather than a pipeline. Lite is there to check whether ZoomInfo's data holds up in your market, not to prospect with.

A credit is spent the moment you export a record, whether that record is a person or a company. Looking at a profile inside the platform costs nothing. Taking it out of the platform is what draws down the balance.

The cost per record isn't flat either. A basic record burns fewer credits than one enriched with technology stack data, org chart relationships and intent signals, so two exports from the same list can carry different prices. On the GTM.AI side there are two separate currencies to track, data credits and AI credits.

Now the calculation that matters most on this page, and both halves of it come from ZoomInfo. Their own blog gives the example of a five-person team exporting 50 contacts a day each, which it puts at roughly 1,000 credits a week. Buyers report the Professional plan including around 5,000 credits a year. Divide one by the other: ZoomInfo's own worked example empties the entry plan in five weeks.

The unit cost follows from the same two numbers. At a reported $15,000 for a reported 5,000 credits, a record leaves the platform at about $3. You'll pull several records before one of them matches your target and is in market, so a prospect worth contacting costs a multiple of that reported $3.
The plan price doesn't cover the whole product. Several pieces that buyers expect to find inside their tier get quoted as separate line items.

When you get ZoomInfo on the phone, ask for a quote itemized line by line instead of a single total. That's the only way you'll see which of these five is already inside your tier and which is about to be added to it, and it's a reasonable thing to ask for before you commit to a year.
Gojiberry checks every account against your ICP and sends you the ones showing buying signals. No credits, no export limit, no annual contract.

This is the part that surprises people who've never signed an enterprise software contract, so it's worth walking through slowly. The contract renews itself. On the anniversary date it restarts for another full twelve months without anyone at your company doing anything, and there's no cancel button in the product to stop it. Ending it takes a formal notification sent before a deadline.

That deadline sits in a notice window that buyers report running 60 to 90 days ahead of the renewal date. Make it concrete: if your contract ends on 1 January, your notice needed to go in back in October or November. Miss the window and you owe another full year, whether the team logs in or not.

The renewal price is also not the price you signed at. Reported increases run 10 to 20 percent year over year, and since the annual invoice is paid upfront, that increase arrives as one payment rather than as a slightly larger monthly line.
Two questions to put to your rep before you sign, in writing:
🔎What happens to the records I've already exported if I don't renew? You want to know whether the contacts sitting in your CRM stay usable.
📥Do unused credits roll over into the next period? If they don't, a balance you didn't spend is a balance you paid for and lost.

Two review platforms give two very different answers, and the gap is wide enough to be worth explaining. ZoomInfo scores 4.5 out of 5 on G2 across 9,384 reviews, a figure ZoomInfo displays itself on its own pricing page. On Trustpilot the score sits far lower: 1.7 out of 5 across 327 reviews, read off the page in August 2026, so a few hundred people rather than a few thousand.

The gap isn't a mystery and it isn't a scandal either. G2 reviews come mostly from people using the product every day, often at companies large enough to have bought it deliberately. Trustpilot reviews come largely from people who tried to cancel. Both scores are real and they aren't measuring the same thing, so read the first for the product and the second for the contract.
Our full ZoomInfo review goes through the product side of that split in more detail.

Yes, and you should assume the first number your rep gives you is a starting point rather than a price. A quote assembled from seats, credits and add-ons has movement in every one of those three parts.
ZoomInfo publishes these same negotiation tips on its own blog, which tells you something about how much room sits inside a first quote.

One thing to weigh before you spend a quarter on this. A negotiated five-figure contract is still a five-figure contract, and for a team of 2 to 10 people, Gojiberry does the job of finding the prospects for $1,188 a year. Compare the two annual spends rather than the feature lists: that's roughly 12 times less than ZoomInfo's reported entry plan, and roughly 28 times less than the median contract at $33,500.
Set your seat count, the volume you'd export in a year and the extras you'd be quoted for, and this gives you the annual band buyers report for that shape of deal.
Estimate your own ZoomInfo quote

Treat the result as a range to budget against. It's built from prices buyers report paying, so it tells you which order of magnitude the conversation will start at, and the extras it counts have no published price at all. Your rep's number is the only quote.
A price you can read before you talk to anyone
Gojiberry costs 99 dollars a month, contacts up to 1,800 prospects for you, and tells you which accounts are showing intent this week. No seat minimum and no twelve-month lock.

The product is built for revenue teams that are already structured: a defined ICP, someone owning operations, and a tooling budget signed off once a year rather than approved purchase by purchase. Remember that sinking feeling when you've blown through your Lusha credits on yet another invalid email or phone number? For a while Lusha was my go-to, but the data gaps, the rapid credit burn and the nagging sense I was missing qualified leads pushed me to a breaking point.

This wasn't about finding a cheaper tool; it was about finding a smarter Lusha alternative, one offering buying-intent signals, deeper company insights and reliable data that wouldn't leave my team chasing ghosts. I tested over a dozen platforms, from Apollo.io and ZoomInfo to Cognism and newer players like Gojiberry. Here's my honest take on the 12 best.
Three quick questions to see which tool actually fits your real outbound needs.

Your answers show you want warm, intent-based leads and a workflow that doesn't burn through cold lists. Gojiberry surfaces buying signals, so your team only reaches out to prospects who are ready to talk.

Your answers suggest Lusha may still cover your core contact-data needs. Still, if you want to move beyond static B2B databases toward warm, intent-based leads, Gojiberry is worth trying as a layer on top.

In the top spot is Gojiberry, a platform that fundamentally shifts the B2B sales paradigm. Instead of merely providing contact data, it functions as an intelligent lead-sourcing engine, a standout Lusha alternative for teams tired of the cold-outreach grind who want to engage prospects already showing strong buying intent.

Gojiberry is an AI-powered, multi-channel prospecting platform. It tracks 30+ buying-intent signals across socials and the web, surfaces leads who are in-market right now, and triggers personalized outreach across channels.

Imagine knowing exactly when a decision-maker at a target account gets promoted, when a company starts hiring for a role your service could replace, or when a prospect engages with a competitor's content. That's the core of Gojiberry's power: it automates the "ear-to-the-ground" research that separates top reps from the rest, delivering a daily feed of warm, high-intent leads into your workflow. While Lusha excels at finding contact details for a list you've already built, Gojiberry helps you build a smarter list from scratch, focusing on the "why" and "when," not just the "who." Teams boost reply rates by over 50% by switching from mass outreach to the highly relevant leads it surfaces.

Key features: real-time signal tracking across socials and the web (job changes, competitor interactions, keyword engagement); automated lead delivery (email, phone, profile) to your CRM, Slack or inbox, saving 10+ hours/week; and high-intent lead scoring so your team prioritizes the most promising prospects. Tip: the sharper your ICP, the more potent the AI recommendations.

For an all-in-one sales-intelligence and engagement platform, Apollo.io is a powerhouse and a strong Lusha alternative that goes way beyond contact data: think of it as your entire sales stack in a box.

It combines 275M+ contacts with sequencing, dialing and analytics, so you can find prospects, enrich data and engage through multi-channel sequences without leaving the platform. Automated persona lists populate themselves with new matching leads in real time.

If Lusha is a targeted tool, ZoomInfo is the enterprise-grade behemoth of B2B data, a top-tier alternative for teams needing the most comprehensive, accurate company and contact information, the gold standard for go-to-market intelligence.
It leverages AI and a contributory network for deep insights: org charts, tech stacks and real-time buyer-intent signals, so you understand the whole buying committee, not just one contact.

For teams prioritizing data compliance and global reach, especially in Europe, Cognism is a premium alternative built around GDPR-compliant contact data, a relief for anyone navigating complex privacy laws.
Its differentiator is accuracy: human-verified mobile numbers (Diamond Data) and Bombora-powered intent data, improving call-to-connect ratios and keeping outreach compliant across EMEA and APAC.

If data accuracy is your top priority, UpLead is an exceptional Lusha alternative, positioning itself as a data-quality leader with a 95% accuracy guarantee, so you spend less time on bounces and more time connecting.
It achieves this through real-time email verification, ensuring every credit is applied to a valid contact, a straightforward tool for building clean lists or enriching your CRM.

To quickly and accurately build an extensive contact list, RocketReach is a good option, with one of the largest databases in the world, hundreds of millions of professional profiles across industries.

It focuses on verified emails and direct dials, often offering multiple graded emails per contact and using AI to point you to the most-active address. Its bulk lookup enriches whole lists in one operation.

Seamless.AI positions itself as a real-time search engine for B2B contacts, using AI to find and verify emails and direct dials, a strong alternative for teams prioritizing speed and AI-powered delivery.
It can recommend contacts and companies fitting your ICP, and its engine cross-references and validates data in real time, a step up from static databases, reducing bounces and wasted calls.

Lead411 balances comprehensive data with powerful buyer-intent signals, integrating with Bombora to serve Growth Intent data so you can spot target accounts researching solutions like yours before they reach out.
Instead of cold prospecting, it helps you warm up outreach by timing, and emphasizes inbox-verified emails to cut bounce rates and protect your domain reputation.

Hunter.io is an excellent, reliable alternative for verified professional email addresses. While others try to be jack-of-all-trades, Hunter excels in email discovery, renowned for simplicity and accuracy.
Its Domain Search instantly shows the common email pattern for a domain and lists known addresses with confidence scores and sources, a clean, straightforward path to your prospect's inbox.
ContactOut belongs on your radar if your main goal is raw data accuracy, especially for emails. It excels at finding verified personal and work emails for contacts on social profiles and GitHub.

Its AI engine cross-references multiple sources for high-confidence contact info, staying laser-focused on data enrichment and directly addressing high bounce rates, a no-frills tool to fuel your existing outreach and CRM.

If your sales process lives on social platforms, Kaspr is a lightweight yet powerful alternative that integrates seamlessly into your prospecting workflow, focusing on verified B2B contact details from social profiles with a single click.
Unlike bloated all-in-one platforms, Kaspr hones in on accurate phone numbers and emails, with an extension that sits right on the profile, built for speed and on-the-fly enrichment.
If your biggest bottleneck is time spent manually capturing and verifying prospect data, LeadIQ is designed to eliminate that friction, built to make prospecting faster and more intelligent.

It captures contacts from your prospecting workflow with a single click, identifies verified work emails and phone numbers, and pushes them to your CRM, a specialized, high-powered prospecting assistant focused on the pre-outreach workflow with real-time verification.

The old "spray and pray" playbook is dead. The real power isn't just finding a contact, it's understanding why you should contact them at this particular moment. Gojiberry surfaces prospects the instant they show buying intent across socials and the web.

Diagnose your biggest pain point. Is it data accuracy? Prioritize a tool with a solid verification guarantee like UpLead or Cognism. Workflow inefficiency? Consolidate with an all-in-one like Apollo.io. A lack of warm leads? That's the most common and deadly problem, so find a tool that uncovers buying intent, like Gojiberry. Align with budget reality: startups should look for flexible plans or a free tier (Kaspr, Hunter.io); scale-ups should think ROI, since a pricier tool that saves each rep hours pays for itself. Test before you invest: give the same list of 10 hard-to-find prospects to two or three tools and see which finds the most accurate direct dials and verified emails.

Apollo.io's free plan. It's generous and gives you an all-in-one platform to find contacts, verify emails and run simple sequences without spending a dime, perfect for building an initial pipeline on a bootstrap budget.

GDPR compliance, full stop. Cognism is built from the ground up with GDPR in mind, and its Diamond Data (human-verified mobiles) makes it the safest, most effective choice for teams serious about selling in Europe.

Look for tools emphasizing real-time verification. Seamless.AI markets itself as a real-time search engine, validating data on the fly rather than pulling from a static database, and UpLead offers a 95% accuracy guarantee with real-time verification at download.

Yes. It's the difference between knocking on random doors and knocking where someone has a welcome mat out. Intent data from tools like Gojiberry, ZoomInfo or Lead411 tells you which companies are actively researching your category, shifting you from a cold motion to a warm, relevant one.

Stop spending your energy on leads that aren't ready to buy. Gojiberry moves beyond simple contact data to deliver intent-driven leads directly to you, so you connect with prospects who are genuinely interested.

Smartlead wins for agencies and for anyone sending past 50,000 emails a month. Lemlist wins for a small team that wants contact data, buying signals and multichannel in one subscription.

Pick Smartlead if you send high volume, run client accounts, or want your tool bill to stay flat while headcount grows. It's unlimited mailboxes on every tier, plus a $29 white-label portal per client, that decide it.

Pick Lemlist if you want one subscription that finds contacts, watches for buying signals and reaches people on email, social, phone, SMS and WhatsApp. It costs more per seat, and there's a lot less for you to assemble.

Pick neither first if your reply rate is low and the sequences look fine. That's a targeting problem, and no sending tool fixes it. B2B contact data rots at roughly 2.1% a month, around 22.5% a year, so a list built in January is a fifth wrong by December. Mindflow lifted its reply rate 31% by changing who it wrote to rather than how.

Both products are self-serve, so we opened both pricing pages on August 5, 2026 and took the tiers, the caps and the add-on rates from the vendors themselves rather than from anyone's comparison page. The review scores come from G2 the same day. That detail matters more than it sounds: Lemlist's site shows 4.7 from 1,396 reviews, one competitor's page quotes 4.4, another quotes 4.7, and G2's own listing says 4.6 for both tools, across 309 reviews for Smartlead and 1,402 for Lemlist. At least three of those numbers are stale. We use the source.

One thing you won't find here: a head-to-head inbox placement number. We haven't run an identical list through both platforms on matched domains, and an invented percentage would be worth less than this sentence admitting it. When we run that test, the numbers land on this page. We pay for our own tools, no vendor read a word of this before publication, and Gojiberry is our product, which is why it loses three of the seven rows above.

Smartlead made one structural choice and everything else follows from it: you pay for the account, not for the people or the mailboxes. Connect five inboxes or five hundred, the invoice is the same. For anyone running domain fleets, that changes the arithmetic completely.

On G2, checked August 5, 2026, Smartlead sits at 4.6 out of 5 across 309 reviews, with 95.6% of reviewers from small businesses. The recurring complaint in critical reviews is how long support takes when a campaign's already running. The recurring praise is the mailbox model and warmup reliability. If you want the volume-tool comparison one level down, we also put Smartlead against Instantly on cold email at scale.

Lemlist runs email, social touches, calls, SMS and WhatsApp from a single campaign, with branching so a prospect who accepts an invite gets a different follow-up from one who ignores it. That much has been true for years. What's new, and what our own page got wrong until today, is everything sitting in front of the sequence.

This page used to get Lemlist wrong on exactly this point, so it's worth being precise about where it stands now. The agents ship on every plan, but the signals are charged per success in credits: 20 credits for a web visit, from 100 for hiring or a job change, 100 for a funding round, and from 400 for a social engagement signal. At one cent a credit, a social signal is $4 apiece. Two hundred of them in a month is $800 on top of the seats.
So the fair framing is this. Lemlist is expanding into data and signals, and doing it well. Its center of gravity is still the sequence, and the intent layer is metered rather than bundled.

On G2, checked the same day, Lemlist also sits at 4.6 out of 5, across 1,402 reviews, with 85.6% from small businesses. Four times the review volume at the same score is worth something on its own. The most common complaint is cost at scale, which is what you'd expect from per-seat billing. For the social-first end of this category, we broke down Lemlist against HeyReach separately.
Six questions, six answers. We name a winner on each one, including the two where our own product doesn't win.

Lemlist, and that surprised us. Its Email plan is priced by volume with unlimited users, so a team of three pays $660 a year on annual billing and gets the 650M database thrown in. Smartlead Pro is $939.60 a year for the same three people. The answer inverts at two thresholds: past 50,000 sends a month you're leaving the Lemlist Email plan, and the moment anyone needs social or calls you're on Multichannel at $87 per seat, which is $3,132 a year for three.

Lemlist, with nothing close behind. Email, social steps, an in-app dialer with VoIP integrations, SMS and a WhatsApp add-on, all branching inside one campaign. Smartlead added SmartDialer for calling, but a genuinely coordinated multichannel sequence isn't what it was built to run.

Lemlist again. Database, email finder, phone finder and intent agents all sit inside the plan, metered by credit. Smartlead sells SmartProspect as a $59 add-on on Base and Pro, free on the Unlimited tiers, and doesn't pretend to do signals. For a three-person team, folding data into the sending tool removes a vendor, an invoice and a sync.

Smartlead. Unlimited inboxes with automatic rotation, unlimited warmup, dedicated sending servers at $39 a month and placement testing from $49 add up to a level of infrastructure control Lemlist doesn't sell. Both include warmup and rotation on every plan, so the question is how far you can push rather than whether the basics are there. Either way the ceiling is the one Google set: since February 2024, bulk senders have to hold a spam complaint rate under 0.3%. We haven't measured placement rates ourselves, so this is a read on architecture.

Lemlist. A rep can open it without help. Pull a list from the database, build a sequence and they'll be sending the same afternoon. Smartlead assumes somebody in the building is comfortable with domains, DNS records and warmup cycles, and its critical reviews cluster around support response times when something breaks mid-campaign. If nobody on your team owns that, the cheaper tool costs you more.

Smartlead, decisively. Branded client workspaces at $29 a month, isolated billing and API tokens per client, and a master inbox that spans all of them. Lemlist has no equivalent portal to hand a client, and the per-seat model means ten clients cost roughly twice as much. That single line is why so many lead-gen agencies end up on Smartlead, and it's rarely a close call.
Every figure below comes from the two pricing pages on August 5, 2026. Smartlead knocks 17% off annual billing. Lemlist knocks off 20%, or 10% if you'd rather pay quarterly.

Unlimited mailboxes and unlimited warmup come with all four. The add-ons that move the invoice are white-label workspaces at $29 per client, SmartServers at $39 each, SmartDelivery from $49, and mailbox provisioning at roughly $4.50 per inbox per month. That's where the real bill lives.

Credits sit on top of all three and only bill on success. A verified email is 5 credits, a phone number is 20, and intent signals run from 20 credits for a web visit to 400 or more for a social engagement. One credit is one cent, and unused credits don't roll over. There's a 14-day trial and no permanent free plan.

One thing to read carefully before the numbers. The Smartlead and Lemlist figures on the first two rows buy an email-only plan, while Gojiberry has a single price that covers signals, enrichment and every channel. Those two rows compare what each team would spend, and they don't compare like for like on scope.

Two lines deserve a note. The team of three on email only is where Lemlist quietly beats Smartlead on price, at $660 against $939.60, and throws in the database. Every vendor comparison we read has this backwards, because they're all still quoting a per-seat Email plan that Lemlist no longer sells. The ten-client agency is the mirror image: $5,214 on Smartlead Unlimited Smart with ten white-label portals, against $10,440 on Lemlist Multichannel with no portal at all.

Gojiberry is $99 a month per workspace, not per seat, with a free plan to start. There's no cheaper tier that strips it back to email, because the signals are the product. That's why the column reads as total spend, and why it answers a different question from the other two, which is what the next section is about.

Outbound has three layers. Find who to contact. Decide when to contact them. Run the contact. Smartlead and Lemlist are both excellent at the third layer, and Lemlist has started biting into the first. Neither one's built around the second.

That distinction shows up in one statistic. Median job tenure in the United States is 3.9 years, with 22% of employees in post under a year. The churn that keeps rotting your list is also the richest signal available to you, and reading it is a different job from sending well.

Gojiberry is an AI-powered multichannel prospecting platform. It tracks more than 30 buying-intent signals across socials and the web, surfaces the leads who are in-market right now, and triggers personalized outreach across channels. It doesn't compete with Smartlead or Lemlist on sending. It answers the question they both assume you've already answered.

For a three-person team, the practical difference is a Monday morning list of twenty accounts that moved last week, each with the reason attached, instead of a spreadsheet of four hundred names that matched a job-title filter. Same sender, same sequence, and an input that isn't guesswork. If you want a hand on the message itself, our free cold email generator is a decent starting point.
You shouldn't have to guess who to contact
Gojiberry watches more than 30 buying signals across socials and the web, checks each account against your ICP, and sends you the ones worth writing to.
Find your line. Take the name at the end of it.
Choosing isn't always the job. Three combinations we see week after week, and what each one is solving for.
High-volume agency

Gojiberry scores and short-lists the accounts per client. Smartlead sends across the mailbox fleet and reports back inside each branded workspace. The agency keeps its margin structure and stops burning domains on cold lists.
SaaS sales team of three
Gojiberry watches the signals and pushes qualified accounts into the CRM. Lemlist runs the email and social sequence off that input, so the personalization has something true to hang on.
Founder doing sales alone
The free Gojiberry plan proves whether the market throws off signals worth chasing. Lemlist Email at $55 a month picks it up from there, with the database bundled so there's no third tool to manage.

of Wispra's weekly demos now come from intent signals rather than cold lists.

Why we're the ones writing this

Every page ranking for this comparison belongs to one of the vendors in it, which is a reasonable thing to be suspicious about, ours included. So here's where we come from. Before Gojiberry, Roman was a cofounder at Coco.ai, and his days were spent prospecting on socials by hand. He'd scroll for a company that had just raised, or a head of sales who'd changed jobs three weeks earlier, and write to that person while the change was still fresh. It worked far better than the lists everyone else was buying.

It also took four hours a day and didn't scale past one person. Gojiberry exists because we tried to automate that one habit. Nobody here looked at the sending-tool market and wanted a slice of it. That's also why this article hands two categories to Smartlead and four to Lemlist. Both of those calls cost us something, and both are what the pricing pages say.

Lemlist, if the three of you send email only. Its Email plan carries unlimited users at $69 a month, or $55 a month on annual billing, so three seats cost the same as one: $660 a year. Smartlead Pro runs $94 a month, or $78.30 annually, which is $939.60 a year. The picture flips the moment you pass 50,000 sends a month, since that's Lemlist's ceiling on the Email plan, or the moment you want social and calls, which move you to Multichannel at $87 per user per year-round seat.

Not natively, and that hasn't changed. Smartlead is an email engine first. It has added SmartDialer for calling and SmartAgents for automation around the edges, but a coordinated sequence that mixes email with social touches and a call step is Lemlist's territory, not Smartlead's. If email is 90% of your motion, that gap costs you nothing. If it isn't, you'll end up paying for a second tool.

Smartlead, on architecture. Every plan carries unlimited mailboxes, unlimited warmup and automatic inbox rotation, and you can add dedicated sending servers at $39 a month each plus placement testing from $49. Lemlist includes lemwarm and inbox rotation on every seat too, but it doesn't sell you the same infrastructure controls. We haven't run a controlled placement test between the two, so treat this as a read on how each product is built rather than a measured result.

For a lot of small teams, yes. Every Lemlist plan now includes a 650M+ contact database with email and phone lookup, and enrichment is billed per success: 5 credits for a verified email, 20 for a phone number, at one cent per credit. That's $0.05 and $0.20. Where it stops short is depth on hard-to-source markets and the quality checks a specialist provider runs. For a team of three prospecting a European mid-market, it usually does the job.

Smartlead, and it isn't close. White-label client workspaces cost $29 a month per client from the Pro plan up, and Unlimited Prime bundles three. Ten client accounts on Unlimited Smart come to $5,214 a year all in. The same ten clients on Lemlist Multichannel, one seat each, come to $10,440 a year with no branded portal to hand over. Agencies pick Smartlead for the portal as much as for the price.

Yes, and our own page used to say otherwise. Lemlist ships Intent Signal Agents on every plan, watching things like a company visiting your site, a funding round, and hiring or job changes. The catch sits in the billing: signals are charged per success in credits. A web visit costs 20 credits, a funding round or a job change starts at 100, and a social engagement signal starts at 400. At one cent a credit, that last one is $4 per signal. It's useful, and it's worth budgeting before you switch it on.

That's the setup most of our customers land on. Gojiberry watches the signals, scores accounts against your ICP and hands you a short list with the reason attached. Smartlead or Lemlist takes it from there and runs the sequence. Nothing gets ripped out, and the sender you already trained your team on keeps doing what it does well.

Start with the free Gojiberry plan to see whether your market is producing signals worth chasing, then pair it with Lemlist Email at $55 a month on annual billing. You get the 650M database, the sequences and lemwarm in one subscription, which matters when there's nobody to assemble a stack. Smartlead Base at $32.50 annually is cheaper, but 6,000 sends a month and no database means you'll be buying data somewhere else.

Smartlead and Lemlist are both good at what they were built for, and this page tells you which one matches your motion. Neither of them decides who's worth the sequence. Point Gojiberry at your ICP, see which accounts moved this week, then hand the list to whichever sender you picked above.

Tell Gojiberry who you sell to and it starts finding qualified prospects for you. Then let Smartlead or Lemlist do what they're good at.

/blog/mailshake-review.description: Mailshake review for 2026: pricing, features, pros and cons, user reviews, and the best alternatives for cold email and outbound.

Mailshake is a sales engagement platform built around cold email sequences, automated follow-ups, a built-in phone dialer and light LinkedIn tasks. It targets small sales teams, founders and agencies who already have a list and want to work through it without fighting the software.

Its strengths are consistent: setup is fast, the sequence builder is one of the simplest in the category, and the dialer sitting inside the same tool is a differentiator most cold email platforms do not have. Its limitation is just as consistent. Mailshake executes outreach, it does not help you decide who to contact. No buying signals, no prospect discovery, no enrichment beyond a separately billed Data Finder.
The verdict: still a good buy for simple email plus calling on a small team, and a poor fit if your reply rates are flat because your list is cold.

Is Mailshake right for you?
3 quick questions, then your outbound tool recommendation. No email required.

Gojiberry, because your bottleneck is the list

Your answers point at who you contact rather than how you contact them. A sequencer will send that same list faster. Gojiberry watches more than 30 buying signals, checks each account against your ICP and hands you the ones worth writing to this week. Keep sending with whatever you already use.
Mailshake fits what you are doing

Email and phone in one sequence, on a team that already knows who it is calling. That is the case Mailshake is built for, and the dialer on Sales Engagement is the reason to pick it over a pure email tool. The question to revisit later is where next quarter's list comes from.
Volume is your constraint, so look at Instantly

Mailshake bills per user with a mailbox allowance per plan. If you plan to run many inboxes at high volume, Instantly charges a flat rate and gives you unlimited sending accounts and unlimited warmup, which is a different economic model entirely.
Personalisation is the product you want, so look at Lemlist

Mailshake's LinkedIn side is deliberately light. If your replies come from how each message is written and where it lands, Lemlist gives you deeper multichannel sequencing, image and video personalisation, and warmup included.
Find people who are ready to buy
Gojiberry finds prospects showing buying intent and gives you their contact details.
Table of contents

Mailshake sits in the execution layer of an outbound stack. You arrive with a list of contacts, and it takes care of everything that happens after that: multi-step cold email sequences, follow-ups that stop when someone replies, LinkedIn tasks, calls, and one dashboard where campaign performance lives.

The reason people stay on it is not a feature. It is that a new rep can build a working sequence on day one without a training session. For a founder or a two-person sales team, that is a real argument.

The limitation follows from the same design. Mailshake assumes the list already exists and that you have a reason to write today. It does not discover prospects, does not enrich them beyond the separately billed Data Finder, does not watch for buying signals, and does not decide anything on your behalf.
Good fit
Less suitable

The dividing line is simple. If your problem is getting messages out cleanly, Mailshake is a good answer. If your problem is that the messages go out cleanly and nobody replies, it is the wrong layer to be shopping in.

This is the core of the product. You import contacts, write a first email, add follow-ups with your own delays, and the sequence runs. Replies stop the sequence automatically, so nobody gets a chase-up after they have already answered, which sounds obvious and is still the thing cheaper tools get wrong.

A/B testing covers subject lines and body copy, and the SHAKEspeare AI assistant drafts a first version from a description of what you sell. Treat it as a starting point rather than a finished email, but it removes the blank page.

Mailshake can add LinkedIn steps to a sequence: connection requests and messages, handled as tasks alongside the email steps. It is enough to run a coordinated email and LinkedIn cadence on a modest volume.

It is not a substitute for a dedicated LinkedIn tool. Compared with platforms built only for that channel, the automation is thinner and the safety controls are less granular. If LinkedIn is your main channel rather than a supporting one, buy for that channel instead.

The built-in dialer is Mailshake's strongest differentiator, and it is the reason to choose it over a pure email sequencer. Calls sit inside the same sequence as the emails, so a rep works one queue instead of switching between an inbox, a spreadsheet and a phone system. Each call outcome lands on the campaign record.
It comes with the Sales Engagement plan, which is the practical reason most teams end up on the top tier.

Lead Catcher pulls replies into one place and lets you filter by status and campaign, which stops a hot answer from disappearing into a shared inbox. Campaign reporting covers opens, clicks, replies, bounces, calls made and tasks completed, in a single readable row per campaign.
It is enough to manage a campaign day to day. Teams used to deeper attribution or cohort analysis will find it shallow.
Mailshake charges per user across three tiers, and the mailbox allowance climbs with the plan. Here is the September 2026 rate card.

One change to note: Mailshake now shows Starter at zero on its own pricing page, where most comparison articles still quote $29 per user. It carries one email address and no sequencing depth, so treat it as a look around rather than a plan.
Do the multiplication before you compare anything

Three reps on Sales Engagement is $297 a month billed monthly, or $255 on annual billing. Five reps on the same plan is $495 a month, or $425 annually. On Email Outreach, three reps come to $147 a month.

Per-user pricing means the bill tracks headcount rather than results. Hire a fourth rep and the line goes up by a full subscription, whether or not that rep sends more. Add a contact database and an enrichment tool, which Mailshake does not include, and a small team's realistic outbound stack lands well above the sticker price.

Trustpilot gives the cleanest public read: 4.8 out of 5 across 100 reviews. That is an overwhelmingly positive profile on a small but real sample, so we will say so plainly rather than manufacture balance.
What users like
What users criticise
The pattern is consistent with the product itself. People who bought Mailshake to send cold email simply and reliably are happy. People who grew into more advanced requirements found the ceiling.

These two answer different questions, and the comparison only makes sense once that is clear. Mailshake is outreach execution. Gojiberry is finding the right prospects, detecting buying signals and then acting on them.

Mailshake works well when you already know who you want to contact. You have the list, the copy and the reason to write. Gojiberry is the relevant tool when the question is different: who should I be contacting right now? It monitors buying-intent signals across socials and the web, filters accounts against your ICP, enriches the contact through a waterfall of providers and turns that into warm leads delivered to your inbox or Slack, with multichannel AI outreach on top.

Choose Mailshake if you already have your lists and mainly need a simple outreach sequencer. Choose Gojiberry if finding high-intent prospects is the bigger problem. Plenty of teams run both, since one sits upstream of the other. We publish our customer results case by case.

Mailshake covers email, phone and basic LinkedIn as one simple sales engagement product, priced per user. Instantly is built around cold email infrastructure and scale: unlimited sending accounts and unlimited warmup on every plan, with flat pricing from $47 a month on Growth, $97 on Hypergrowth and $358 on Light Speed, metered on emails sent and contacts stored rather than on people.

Choose Instantly if email volume across many inboxes is the strategy. Choose Mailshake if two or three reps need email and calling in one place. Our guide to email outreach automation tools and what they cost covers the wider field.

Lemlist is the stronger comparison for teams that want advanced multichannel personalisation. Image and video personalisation, deeper LinkedIn sequencing, warmup included rather than bolted on, and more AI woven through the sequence builder. It also bills per user, from around $79 per user per month on Email Pro and around $109 on Multichannel Expert, with roughly 20 percent off annually.

Choose Lemlist if the message and the channel mix are what win your deals. Choose Mailshake if you want straightforward sequencing plus a dialer and no learning curve. We put Lemlist head to head with the volume side of the market in Smartlead vs Lemlist.
Get warm leads for your business
Gojiberry finds high-intent prospects and sends them straight to your inbox or Slack.

Yes, for a specific buyer. Mailshake remains a good choice for small teams running straightforward cold email, for anyone who also needs calling in the same sequence, and for buyers who value simplicity over configurability. It does what it promises, it is well supported, and nobody on your team will need training to use it.

It is much less compelling for teams that need prospect discovery, buying intent, enrichment, signal-based targeting or more autonomous outbound. Those are not gaps in the roadmap, they are outside what the product sets out to do.

Mailshake helps you automate the outreach. Modern outbound platforms increasingly help you decide who is worth contacting in the first place. That is the distinction that should drive your decision, because a flat reply rate on a technically healthy campaign is almost never a sequencer problem. Sending the same cold list faster produces the same numbers, sooner. This is where a signal layer such as Gojiberry belongs in the stack, sitting upstream of whatever you send with.

Yes. Sequences, automated follow-ups that stop on reply, A/B testing and Lead Catcher cover what a small team needs, and the setup is fast enough to launch on day one. Where it stops short is targeting: it sends to the list you bring, and does nothing to build or qualify that list.

Mailshake lists Starter as free with one email address. Email Outreach costs $49 per user per month, or $45 on annual billing. Sales Engagement, which carries the phone dialer, is $99 per user per month, or $85 annually. Three reps on Sales Engagement come to $297 a month billed monthly.

For simple cold email and calling on a small team, yes. It is reliable, easy and well supported. For teams that need buying intent, enrichment or signal-based targeting, no, because Mailshake automates the sending and leaves the harder question, who to contact and when, entirely to you.

Instantly for high-volume cold email, priced flat with unlimited sending accounts. Lemlist for multichannel personalisation across email and LinkedIn. Gojiberry for signal-driven outbound, where buying intent and ICP filtering decide who enters the sequence rather than a static import.

Not in the usual sense. Mailshake says it collects payment up front rather than running a trial period, and offers onboarding, deliverability training and support resources instead. The free Starter plan lets you look around with one email address, and Data Finder has a free tier of 50 one-time credits.
Stop sending to lists that were never warm
Tell Gojiberry who you sell to and it starts surfacing companies showing buying signals. Keep Mailshake for the sending, we handle the who.

Most teams leave for one of five reasons, price being the loudest. The quieter one is data: median job tenure in the US runs 3.9 years, with 22% of workers in post under a year, so a chunk of any list you inherited already points at people who've moved on.
Our guide to B2B sales automation covers where each layer sits in the stack.

These twelve don't do the same job. Three are agents running outbound end to end, seven are platforms where a rep drives, one is a set of parts you wire together. The first starts earlier, by deciding who's worth a message. The order runs from closest swaps to cheapest pieces.

How we built this list. Every price was read off the vendor's own pricing page in September 2026. We ignored the figures circulating in comparison posts, several of which describe a model that doesn't exist any more, and where a vendor gates its numbers we say so.

What you won't find is a scorecard of reply rates. We haven't run one campaign on one list through all twelve, and a made-up percentage would be worth less than this sentence admitting it. We pay for every plan ourselves, no vendor read this first, and Gojiberry is our product, which is why it's first and why we say where it loses.

Gojiberry watches for the moment a company starts looking, then reaches the people inside it. It tracks 30+ buying-intent signals across socials and the web, scores them against your ICP, and runs the outreach. You're buying the list; sending is what happens next.
Pro is $99 a month for the account, not per seat, with two agents and up to 1,800 prospects contacted. There's a free start.
We won't pretend to be the hands-off agent AiSDR sells. We make sure the 400 people you contact are worth contacting: GTE Localize booked 100+ meetings that way, and you can read how.
11x runs Alice, an agent that researches accounts, writes the touches, sends them, and handles what comes back. Outbound happens without anyone opening a sequence builder.
Growth starts at $3,750 a month on annual billing. Pro and Enterprise aren't published, they're quoted.
It removes more manual work than anything here, and it's a first-year commitment costing what a junior rep does.
Artisan bundles a 300M+ database with Ava, an agent that builds sequences and runs them. Autopilot sends alone, copilot waits for approval.
The Employee package lists around $600 a month billed annually, and you won't see volume pricing without a call.
One vendor instead of three. Then you notice the annual term, and that what's published is a floor.
Agent Frank pulls prospects from a 500M+ index, writes in your tone, sends and follows up. It works in 20+ languages, which counts once your market stops being English-only.
Frank starts at $599 a month billed quarterly for 1,000 active contacts, and you'll get two months free annually.
No buying signals sit underneath, so Frank writes beautifully to whoever you've pointed him at. Plenty of teams take that trade.
Reply.io has run sequences since 2014, with Jason AI added on top. Email, calls, SMS and social share one cadence, and a rep signs off.
Email Volume opens at $49 per user a month, Multichannel at $89, plus channel add-ons. Jason AI's separate, from $500.
Human oversight is where it wins. Per-seat arithmetic is where it loses.
Regie.ai stacks AI agents on a 220M+ database, with sequencing, intent prioritization and a dialer. It's aimed at sales floors rather than founders.
AI SEP lists at $180 per user a month with a ten-seat minimum, so the real floor's $1,800 a month.
The seat minimum decides this one. Below ten reps with nobody owning ops, the contract costs more than the pipeline it'd find you.
Amplemarket puts contact data, buying signals and sequencing behind one login, with an AI copilot reviewing campaigns. Teams that move here retire three or four subscriptions.
Startup is $600 a month for two seats, annual billing only. Growth and Elite aren't published at all.
Nothing here folds more tools into one contract, and nothing here asks a two-person team for a bigger bet before they've tested it.
Apollo is the first subscription many small teams buy: database, sequences, dialer and CRM sync in one workspace. A rep drives all of it.
Basic runs $49 per seat on annual billing, Professional $79, Organization $119 with three seats minimum. Pay monthly and you'll add 20%.
It's the cheapest route to data and sending on one subscription, if somebody has the hours to work it.
Instantly exists to get cold email delivered at volume. Unlimited sending accounts and warmup come with every plan, so the bill tracks sends rather than headcount.
Growth is $47 a month for 5,000 sends, Hypergrowth $97, Light Speed $358. The lead database isn't bundled, it's billed apart.
Nothing here moves more email for less money. Then you add credits and the CRM module, and $47 lands nearer $125.
Clay is a table where each column calls a data provider or an AI agent. 150+ sources sit behind it, and nothing sends until you attach a sender.
Launch is $185 a month with 2,500 data credits and Growth is $495. New customers can't buy the old tiers.
Ceiling is the highest here. Floor is a person who wants to build.
Smartlead sells deliverability: unlimited mailboxes, warmup, inbox rotation and a master inbox, pointed at agencies and high-volume senders.
Base is $39 a month for 2,000 leads and 6,000 sends, Pro $94, Unlimited Smart $174, Prime $379. You aren't charged per inbox.
Nothing here protects a sending reputation better, and nothing here cares less whether the list deserved the send.
Snov.io folds an email finder, verifier, drip campaigns and a light CRM into one cheap subscription. Seats are unlimited on every paid plan.
Starter is $39 a month for 1,000 credits and Pro starts at $99 for 5,000. Social automation isn't included, at $69 per slot.
Price is the whole argument. A three-person team gets a full outbound loop for less than one Apollo seat, and depth is what they pay for it.
Monthly starting prices, taken from each vendor directly in September 2026. Seat minimums and annual-only terms are flagged where they move the floor.

For warm, high-intent leads, it's us. Claiming otherwise would be odd, since finding them is why Gojiberry exists. Wispra now sources 60% of its weekly demos from intent signals, which you can see broken down here.

For a fully autonomous rep, 11x if the budget and security review are there, Artisan if you'd rather one vendor carried the data. On budget, Instantly wins on the sticker and Snov.io once you count seats. For all-in-one prospecting, Apollo, whose free plan lets you find out before committing.
For multichannel with oversight, Reply.io. For personalization, Clay, if somebody enjoys building. For deliverability at volume, Smartlead. For a bigger SDR floor, Regie.ai past ten seats.
Want better leads before you start sending?
Gojiberry surfaces prospects who are in-market this week and enriches them before they reach your sequences.
Four questions settle most of it, and the last decides less than people expect.

Your stack, ICP and volume matter more than any feature table. Volume without targeting is also the shortest path to Google's 0.3% spam complaint threshold, which bulk senders have had to stay under since February 2024. Our walkthrough on automating sales prospecting orders those decisions.

Smartlead's Base plan and Snov.io's Starter both open at $39 a month, and Instantly's Growth at $47. None of the three includes an agent. Gojiberry's Pro plan is $99 for the whole account, with nothing charged per seat.

A team of two to ten wants flat pricing and no seat minimums, which points at Gojiberry, Instantly, Smartlead and Snov.io. Regie.ai's ten-seat minimum and Amplemarket's annual-only contract rule both out at that size.
Not the whole job. Agents handle research, first touches and follow-ups well, and they're weak on objections. Teams that get value from them move reps toward closing rather than cutting heads.

Instantly or Smartlead, and it's close. Smartlead's rotation and master inbox are more mature, Instantly is cheaper at entry. Both make you bring a list, and B2B contact data decays around 2.1% a month.

Reply.io if you want a rep approving each step, Gojiberry if you'd rather the agent coordinate email and social itself. Reply's add-ons push the real per-seat cost near $187, so run that against your headcount.

Apollo, Clay and Snov.io all run free tiers, and each one's a demo rather than a working plan. Gojiberry starts free without a card, AiSDR has no trial at all. Our roundup of email outreach automation tools covers each tier.

You've got a team, and the sending was never the hard part. Picking who deserves the message is. That's the part we built.

You're solo and the price decides it, so Octopus CRM is the right answer and we're not going to pretend otherwise. It undercuts Dux-Soup and does close to the same job. Come back when the question turns into who to message.
